name: AI Video Avatar Studio - Orchestrated Generation and Adversarial QA
description: Generates cinematic AI video avatars that explain difficult concepts. Owner-approved, config-conformant, adversarially reviewed.

options.systemMessage:
You write on-camera scripts for a Senior Agile Delivery Lead explaining hard technical ideas from direct experience.

ABSOLUTE PROHIBITIONS - violating any one of these fails the run:
- No apology, no self-deprecation, no defensiveness, no hedging about competence. Never: sorry, apologies, unfortunately, I am afraid, disclaimer, I am not an expert, I might be wrong, bear with me, hopefully, to be honest, I hope this helps, I am just, I am only, please forgive.
- No boasting, no superlatives, no marketing register. Numbers over adjectives. Never: world-class, cutting-edge, revolutionary, best-in-class, passionate, guru, ninja, game-changing.
- No stage directions, no speaker labels, no markdown, no emoji, no bracketed notes. Output spoken words only.

REQUIRED SHAPE:
1. Open with the counter-intuitive claim in one sentence. No preamble, no greeting.
2. Name precisely why the concept is hard - the specific thing that trips competent people up.
3. Ground it in the supplied experience with at least one concrete, checkable detail.
4. Close on the operational consequence: what someone should now do differently.

REGISTER: declarative, calm, evidence-led. The authority comes from precision, never from volume. Speak as someone who has run the system, not someone describing it from outside.

LENGTH: exactly the words a measured speaker delivers in the target duration - budget 150 words per minute, so a 10 second script is about 25 words. Never exceed the budget; an over-length script desynchronises the avatar.

Also return a motion_prompt describing head-and-shoulders framing with restrained movement, and a negative_prompt listing artefacts to suppress.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample: {"title":"Idempotency is a design requirement","script":"Spoken words only, no stage directions.","motion_prompt":"Head and shoulders, minimal gesture, steady eye contact","negative_prompt":"text overlays, captions, extra people, hands near face, camera shake","concept_difficulty":"why this concept is genuinely hard","evidence_line":"the concrete experience the claim rests on","word_count":118}

options.systemMessage:
You are an independent adversarial reviewer. You did not produce this work and you owe it no charity. A different model family wrote the script; your job is to try to break the result, not to bless it.

RULES OF EVIDENCE:
- The measured container facts are the only physical evidence you have. Treat them as authoritative and treat every other statement as a claim.
- You cannot see the video. Never assert anything about what the footage looks like. Say what the measurements prove and what they leave unproven.
- Return CONFIRMED only if every conformance defect list is empty AND the script satisfies the content contract. Any single defect means REJECTED.
- A warning is not a defect, but list it as an advisory note.
- If voice_is_cloned is false, that is an advisory note, not a blocking defect - but state plainly that the asset must not be presented as Vikram speaking.

WHAT TO ATTACK IN THE SCRIPT:
1. Apologetic, defensive or hedging register anywhere. The deterministic gate catches literal phrases; you catch the same posture expressed in words the ban-list missed.
2. Boasting, superlatives or marketing language. The site rule is numbers over adjectives, every claim traceable.
3. A claim that does not follow from the stated grounding experience. Unsupported authority is a blocking defect.
4. A concept explained so loosely that a competent practitioner would learn nothing. Vagueness dressed as depth is a blocking defect.
5. Length that will desynchronise the avatar against the stated duration.

Be specific. Quote the offending span. A review that says the work looks good without citing a measured field or a quoted span is itself a failure: in that case return REJECTED with the reason that you had no evidence to inspect.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample: {"verdict":"CONFIRMED","confidence":0.0,"blocking_defects":["one sentence each"],"advisory_notes":["one sentence each"],"evidence":"the specific measured field or quoted script span the verdict rests on"}

parameters.content:
## 1 - Brief and preflight

Authenticated form (n8n user auth, execute permission required) so only you can start a run.

Three preflight probes run before anything is spent: the OpenRouter key, the ElevenLabs voice, and the ElevenLabs subscription. In ELEVENLABS_LIVE mode the run halts if can_use_instant_voice_cloning is false - the pay-as-you-go plan limit that blocks synthesising from an Instant Voice Clone. Every failure halts here with the exact remediation and zero spend.

## 2 - Plan, script, register gate

The planner holds the model capability matrix probed live from GET /api/v1/videos/models. It snaps duration to each model supported list, picks the highest resolution at or below target, routes anything short of target through flux-video-upscale (3x ceiling), derives a stable seed from the concept so identical inputs reproduce the run, and refuses to dispatch above your spend ceiling.

The register gate is deterministic, not a model opinion: literal ban-lists for apologetic and boastful phrasing plus a hard word-count ceiling at 150 wpm.

## 3 - Auto-approve (adversarial QA sole gate)

Nothing has been generated and nothing spent at this point. The form shows the script, voice source, resolved per-model parameters, the seed and the exact estimated cost. DECLINE ends the run cleanly.

## 4 - Three voice sources

ELEVENLABS_LIVE synthesises the new script - needs a Starter plan or above.
ELEVENLABS_ARCHIVE refetches an existing history item, which is your real cloned voice and works on pay-as-you-go today.
MODEL_NATIVE lets the video model speak; that is NOT your voice and is flagged as such all the way through to the delivery note.

OpenRouter rejects data: URIs on input_references - HTTPS only - so the MP3 is stored in the avatar_studio_assets data table and served by this workflow own public webhook. No external storage.

## 5 - Parallel generation and polling

Every selected model is dispatched in one pass, so all renders run concurrently server-side. The poll loop folds all jobs each cycle and only continues when every job is terminal, with a 90-poll ceiling so a stuck provider cannot run forever.

## 6 - Measurement and adversarial review

The MP4 is parsed byte-level in pure JS - moov, tkhd, stsd, avcC, mdhd, stsz - to recover real width, height, fps, codec, H.264 profile and chroma format. There is no ffmpeg in the n8n container, and the provider own claims are not evidence.

The measured facts go to a reviewer on a different model family from the writer. It must cite a measured field or quote a span; a review with no evidence is itself a failure and returns REJECTED.

## 7 - Delivery chain

Test (conformance) - adversarial auto-publish - Push and Deploy (dispatches the existing CI and Deploy workflow on the repo) - production verification - feedback record.

Failure routes to the refinement loop: named defects are fed back into the script brief and the run repeats, maximum 3 attempts, then halts honestly rather than shipping drift.

## Asset host

Public GET endpoint that serves the cloned-voice MP3 to OpenRouter. Separate trigger, same workflow. Unknown tokens get a clean 404 rather than a broken binary response.

## Credentials to set once

1. OpenRouter - Avatar Studio -> OpenRouter API credential, your sk-or-v1 key. Used by the video endpoint, both agents and the download.

2. ElevenLabs API -> Custom Auth (templated). Template:
{"headers":{"xi-api-key":"{{api_key}}"}}
The key must start with sk_. A key ID is not a key.

3. Resend API -> Custom Auth (templated). Template:
{"headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer {{api_key}}"}}

4. GitHub PAT -> Custom Auth (templated). Same Bearer template. Needs actions:write on Victordtesla24/forgotten-mistory.

No secret is stored in any node parameter.
